text:
Matthew Schaefer won the Calder last season at 18, and now he's found another gear. He plays 26:41 a night for the Islanders, two minutes more than as a rookie, and has 26 points in 23 games, up from 0.72 a game to 1.13. Our numbers call it a breakout, and Evolving-Hockey already had him 23rd among all defensemen in wins above replacement as a rookie.

Some of the goal total will come back to earth. He has nine goals on 6.4 expected, and that finishing rate rarely lasts for a defenseman. The rest looks sturdy: the Islanders take 54% of the five-on-five expected goals with him on, 5.8 points better than without him, and he carries the puck into the zone on half his entries in Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking. He ranks 31st in the league in wins added. Our range projects 65 to 89 points. The headlines this month have been about his mother, Jennifer, and the ladybugs that keep her close. That part needs no numbers.
